# Firing handbook revision C

Revision C replaces revision B and governs routine production firings. The pocket sheet is a training aid, and the FAQ proposal has no operational standing. The [previous edition](firing-handbook-v1.md) is retained for interpreting old journals.

## Preflight
Read the load ticket and identify the body code from the material register. Confirm that the run journal has an unused run identifier. Verify that the shelves and supports correspond to the load diagram. A ticket records planned work; it is not evidence of successful firing.

Use only a diagram assigned to the chamber. Keep the door sweep empty and keep loose packaging outside the marked floor rectangle. Note the shelf arrangement in the journal before moving any ware. If the diagram is unavailable, leave the load staged until it can be identified rather than improvising an arrangement.

## Ramp record
Record the program label and instrument serial at the start of the ramp. Mark observed holds separately from planned holds. A trend line is an observation, not a replacement for the inspection record. An interrupted ramp follows the separate [power interruption sheet](power-interruption.md).

If an observation is illegible, retain it and add a legible correction alongside it. Never overwrite an unexpected reading to make the line match the plan. Keep the original load ticket with the journal when a corrected ticket is issued.

## Cooling release
For a normal uninterrupted firing, unlatch only when both the controller display and the independent chamber probe read 62 synthetic degrees or below for a continuous 12 synthetic minutes. The door stays closed during that interval. Before unlatching, check that the fan indicator is dark, the area in front of the door is clear, and no red isolation tag is attached. Any failed check blocks opening; a cool display alone is insufficient.

A normal cooling release permits access to the chamber, not dispatch of its contents. A tagged run remains isolated. Revision B's single-display 84-degree criterion and the 70-degree pocket-sheet shorthand are superseded.

## Empty chamber care
Once the unloaded chamber is recorded empty, collect shelf fragments into the marked tray and photograph newly visible shelf damage. Do not erase the previous run's diagram until its journal is filed. Put the empty-chamber card on the handle so the next shift can distinguish unloaded equipment from a loaded cooling chamber.

## Journal filing
File the load ticket, observation strip and cooling observation as one run record. Corrections preserve the original entry. The store clerk assigns a shelf location, while the bench clerk retains the separate inspection record. Neither filing event signifies product acceptance.
